PullRequest.Title: sessions: add appearance tools and chat background skill
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

Adds agent-driven chat background customization in the Agents window:

- `setChatBackground` applies an image, the Codicons preset, no background, or an image layout through the existing background service. Image files are validated, copied into per-profile local storage, and retained while referenced by settings or the recent-image list.
- `getThemeColors` returns the effective theme name, color scheme, and 18 prominent color roles with token IDs and resolved values, including overrides, tinting, transparency, and unavailable values.
- The built-in `generate-chat-background` skill owns the image-generation workflow and optional pattern/atmospheric design guidance. User preferences take precedence; the setter's description stays focused on mechanics.
- `chat.agentSessions.appearanceTools.enabled` gates both tools and the built-in skill. It is advanced, enabled by default, and experiment-controlled with `mode: 'auto'`. Disabling it updates tool registration, slash-command discovery, and agent-host skill forwarding without removing existing backgrounds or manual controls.

The shared prompts service gains a built-in-change notification hook so the setting can invalidate discovery caches without Sessions-specific dependencies in the workbench layer. Accessibility help and focused regression tests are included.

## How to test

1. Open the desktop Agents window and confirm the Appearance tool group exposes Get Theme Colors and Set Chat Background.
2. Ask for the current palette, then use `/generate-chat-background` or ask the agent to generate and apply an image. Verify image, preset, removal, and layout-only requests; backgrounds remain specific to the active dark/light color scheme and hidden in high contrast.
3. Set `chat.agentSessions.appearanceTools.enabled` to `false`. Confirm both tools and the built-in skill disappear, stale calls fail, and the existing background/manual controls still work. Re-enable it without reloading.

The background setter is desktop-only. Remote image paths use the invoking chat's working-directory context; if the host invokes the tool without that context, absolute paths resolve on the client machine.

## Validation

Before updating the branch from `main`:

- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only` — passed.
- The following focused selection — **156 passed**:

```sh
./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot \
  --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/appearanceTools.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/chatBackgroundTool.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/getThemeColorsTool.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/electron-browser/chatBackgroundTool.contribution.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/node/chatBackgroundSkill.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/common/promptSyntax/service/promptsService.test.ts
```

After merging `main`:

- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed with available installed dependencies.
- `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=ACM -z origin/main...HEAD -- '*.ts' | xargs -0 npm run eslint --` — passed for all 17 changed TypeScript files.
- `npm run valid-layers-check` — passed.
- `npm run install-fast` — blocked by registry authentication (`E401`). `npm_config_offline=true npm run install-fast` also failed because the upstream Codex package was not cached.
- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only` — blocked by the upstream Copilot SDK/runtime version mismatch after the unsuccessful dependency refresh. The post-merge unit-test rerun therefore did not execute; CI must validate the merged dependency set. No credentials or registry settings were changed.

Earlier live checks used the running Code OSS Agents window to invoke the registered theme tool, verify both tools in the Appearance group, and generate/apply several background variants with screenshots. Full integration/smoke suites and a live remote-host image flow were not run.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The call path is explicit and fully awaited: importImage writes the content-addressed file and returns created=true; cancellation at lines 256 or 269 throws through invoke; neither cancellation branch deletes the file, and the sole pruning caller is after successful apply. Repository search finds no other owner or cleanup call for agentsChatBackgrounds. Exact prevalence is uncertain, but retention and scaling are deterministic.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Imported image files and their bytes in per-profile local storage.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Retained storage grows linearly with the number of distinct invocations canceled after import, at up to 25 MB per invocation; a future prune also performs metadata/filter/delete work proportional to the accumulated file count.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Unbounded retained filesystem storage and eventual extra metadata/delete I/O when a later prune scans the accumulated files.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR there was no agent-driven import folder or tool path that copied images into profile storage, so canceling a background operation could not strand these content-addressed copies.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Background-tool invocations now copy non-known source images into per-profile storage before decoding/applying them, but a cancellation after the copy aborts before any cleanup or pruning runs.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added prepareImage path assigns a newly copied import, then added RIGHT line 256 throws on cancellation without deleting it; the only targeted delete is inside the later decode-error catch, while pruneImportedImages is awaited only after apply succeeds at line 221.
Findings.Title: Clean up imports when image preparation is cancelled
Findings.Impact: Canceling an image-background tool call after its copy finishes (or while image decode is in progress) leaves an unreferenced file of up to 25 MB in profile storage. Repeated canceled generation/apply attempts with distinct images permanently grow disk usage until a later successful background operation happens after the grace period; if the user stops using the tool, those files are never reclaimed.
Findings.Evidence: importImage reads up to MAX_IMAGE_SIZE (25 MB) and writes the content to agentsChatBackgrounds. prepareImage then checks cancellation before decode and again after decode. Only the decode-error catch deletes imported.created; cancellation is rethrown by invoke. pruneImportedImages is called only after the switch in apply, which canceled preparation never reaches, and no other pruneImportedImages/agentsChatBackgrounds cleanup exists.
Findings.Recommendation: Track whether importImage created the file and delete that new copy in a cancellation/failure cleanup path before rethrowing (while preserving reused files and files that were successfully applied); alternatively give the import folder an independent startup/disposal cleanup owner so reclamation does not depend on a later successful invocation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Apply a local or remote image through setChatBackground
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The tool result waits for source validation, optional full read/hash/copy, browser image decode, configuration/storage updates, and a local import-folder prune. All are on the invocation critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stat and read the local or remote source image.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One stat per invocation; for a non-known image, one full read of up to 25 MB. Remote-agent paths route that read through the registered remote file provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The pre-diff application had manual background selection but no agent tool importing an invoking chat's local/remote image.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Validation and the full source read must complete before the image can be applied.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create/reuse a content-addressed image copy in per-profile global storage.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: For each new content hash, one destination existence check and at most one write of up to 25 MB; repeated identical content avoids the write.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No agentsChatBackgrounds import store existed before this diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The copy completes before decode and apply. If cancellation is observed afterward, the new copy remains retained.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load and decode the copied image through a browser img element.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One browser image decode for each image invocation, including reused imports.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Manual rendering decoded configured backgrounds, but there was no extra tool-time validation decode.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Decode and dimension measurement must complete before configuration changes are applied.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist background URI/layout and recent-image metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One image preference update and optional one layout update; recent-image storage is updated once for an image.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same service operations existed for manual controls; the diff adds an agent-driven caller.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These updates are awaited before the result and trigger existing background renderers.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Scan and prune per-profile imported images.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One folder existence check and one metadata-resolving directory scan per successful invocation, then one delete per stale unreferenced file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No import folder or pruning scan existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Pruning is awaited before returning the tool result.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number and byte size of distinct generated/source images, especially invocations canceled after copying; successful steady state is roughly five recent images plus dark/light preferences and the one undo-preserved image.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A single Sequencer serializes all setChatBackground invocations in the window. The prune issues deletions concurrently with Promise.all; normally effective cardinality is bounded by recent/configured images, but stranded canceled imports can enlarge that burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A new source image is fully read and hashed to derive a content-addressed destination; an existing destination avoids the write but not the source read/hash. A path already under the import folder or referenced by preferences/recent history bypasses import and hashing. Recent references are capped at five, plus the two scheme preferences. There is no negative cache. Cancellation after creating a new destination leaves it outside those references and outside any independent cleanup lifecycle.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the write, both later cancellation checks, successful-only prune caller, and absence of any other cleanup owner were directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Frequency of users canceling during the post-copy/pre-apply window and typical generated image size are uncertain; the deterministic upper bound is 25 MB retained per distinct canceled attempt.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable cleanup-lifecycle regression: newly created copies can survive cancellation indefinitely and accumulate linearly.

Scenarios.Scenario: Apply Codicons, clear a background, or change image layout
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The result waits for one configuration update and then the same import-folder existence/metadata scan; layout-only calls also validate that an image is configured.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist the selected preset, removal, or layout through the existing background service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One configuration persistence operation per preset/clear/layout call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Manual commands invoked the same service; the agent tool is new.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before rendering state and tool output progress.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Prune the current profile's imported-image folder.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One folder existence check and, when present, one metadata directory resolution plus stale-file deletes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited even though preset/layout changes do not import an image.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Count of children in the current profile's import folder.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The same global Sequencer serializes preset and layout calls; prune deletions can fan out only over stale folder children.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No meaningful cache is involved. Referenced-image lookup reads bounded recent/configured metadata; pruning uses the current folder contents.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the call path and serialization; low concern because normal cardinality is bounded and infrequent.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The folder scan is usually small because recent/configured references are bounded, and preset/layout calls are user/agent initiated rather than hot UI events.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: the filesystem work is on the critical path but normally bounded and infrequent; abnormal folder growth is covered by the cancellation-retention finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: Read the current Agents-window theme palette
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Eighteen theme-token lookups, color formatting, and a small JSON serialization occur synchronously before returning the tool result.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Invocations are independent, but calls are explicit model tool calls and each performs fixed-size work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache or polling is added; every explicit invocation takes a fresh in-memory theme snapshot.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the complete invoke implementation is fixed-cardinality and contains no I/O/IPC/network boundary.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact invocation frequency depends on agent use, but work is fixed at 18 roles and a small result.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: fixed, small in-memory CPU/allocation work with no scaling collection or expensive boundary.

Scenarios.Scenario: Disable or re-enable appearance tools and built-in skill discovery
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The configuration change itself emits synchronously; discovery consumers refresh asynchronously/lazily through existing cached promises. When requested, skill/slash discovery must list configured sources and parse prompt files before those surfaces update.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invalidate and recompute skill/slash-command discovery when the built-in skill gate changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: On each appearance-setting toggle that has active consumers, one coalesced skill-location discovery across user/local/extension/plugin/built-in sources; skill and slash-command projections can parse the discovered skill files through existing bounded reads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The appearance setting and its built-in-change event did not exist; normal file/plugin/configuration events already used the same discovery paths.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before updated slash-command and skill lists are delivered, but not on startup/render/input unless the user changes this setting.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of discovered prompt/skill files and source folders, once per appearance-setting change with active consumers.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Skill and slash-command discovery share the cached location listing; per-file parsing uses the existing queueDiscoveryRead limiter rather than unbounded reads.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The setting event invalidates only the skill location cache and the existing CachedPromise instances for skills/slash commands. The shared listPromptFiles promise coalesces concurrent skill-location scans once file-locator events have initialized caching; subsequent reads are warm until another discovery event. No negative-cache behavior changed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for invalidation and cache sharing; high confidence that frequency is setting-change scoped.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Repositories can have many skills, but appearance-setting toggles are rare and the location scan is coalesced; no evidence moves this work onto a recurring UI path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the diff intentionally refreshes discovery once per rare setting change, with existing cache coalescing and read limiting.

Scenarios.Scenario: Start the Agents window and register/gate appearance tools
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Registration is off the startup-critical early phases and does not perform image/theme I/O. Dynamic tool-set membership reacts to tool registration through existing infrastructure.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed two tools and one tool set per Agents window.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous registration/disposal on a single setting observable; no task fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Tool instances and static descriptions are created once at the Eventually workbench phase. observableConfigValue reuses the same tool instance and only replaces its registration when the setting changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from contribution constructors and tests asserting one reused tool instance.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: fixed-size eventually-phase work with no expensive boundary.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render and update the configured chat background across active chat views
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Configuration/theme events synchronously recompute small context-key state and notify existing renderers. Applying an image sets CSS background properties on the existing main renderer and sticky replicas.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Visible chat/sticky replicas and configured image dimensions; neither cardinality is changed by the service additions.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Renderer updates run through the existing event path; each visible chat can own a sticky replica, but the diff does not alter replica cardinality or resize scheduling.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The background service reads the capped recent-image metadata and two scheme preferences on demand; no new long-lived in-memory collection is retained.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for unchanged renderer path and bounded metadata reads.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Decoded-image memory depends on image dimensions, but arbitrary user-selected backgrounds and renderer behavior predate this PR; the diff does not establish a new renderer multiplicity or dimension regression independently of the new tool.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: service additions expose configured/reference metadata; existing renderer fan-out and image decoding are not materially amplified by the changed service code.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 18 changed files and all diff pages. Traced image import, remote/local file boundaries, configuration/storage writes, pruning, image rendering, tool registration, palette serialization, and prompt-discovery cache invalidation. Submitted one medium-confidence-severity cleanup lifecycle finding (high mechanism confidence): copied images survive cancellation and can accumulate indefinitely. No performance regression fix requiring blame was identified.
